name: Open Items
rows: FY2027 (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027) · Form 1120 estimated tax · EFTPS tax period 06/2027 · USD · EIN XX-XXX7890 (demonstration) · as of 2026-11-08
DRAFT PLAN · NOTHING PAID · human review required

The October 15 payment of $1,324.70 (EFT 270988315406) went to tax period 12/2026, the calendar-year habit; HANGS's tax year ends June 30, so FY2027 is 06/2027. Until it is moved, the 1st installment is $1,324.70 short: $6.10 of penalty to November 8, $15.50 by December 15, and the December payment would go first to the 1st installment. A person (the controller, or with Form 2848 on file) asks the IRS to move it to 06/2027 as of October 15.

HANGS is a large corporation for FY2027 because FY2024 taxable income was $1,182,400.00, from the controller's summary, figured without NOL carryovers. A person confirms it against the FY2024 return as filed. The rule costs HANGS the prior-year base after the 1st installment: the regular 2nd installment recaptures $14,609.23 ($32,381.15 in all). The annualized method brings it to $18,308.87; paying $3,162.70 again, as the controller asks, would leave $15,146.17 short.

The annualized method rests on $255,613.93 for July to September 2026 (book income of $205,803.93 from the reviewed, not audited, quarterly figures, plus the tax adjustments) and on projected figures for 6 and 9 months ($704,263.93, $1,104,823.93). The NOL deduction is taken after annualizing, at 80% of the annualized income, as an extraordinary item on line 23b; a person confirms that treatment under Regulations section 1.6655-2(f). Refresh the 3rd and 4th installments when the six and nine months close. Form 2220 with Schedule A goes with the FY2027 return.

The $1,838.00 counts toward the 1st installment only when the FY2026 return is filed electing it on line 37a. That return is a draft, extended to April 15, 2027, with open items of its own (the excavator's special allowance, the officer pay resolution, the related-party contract). If its tax changes, so do the $12,650.79 base of the 1st installment and the credit. The date the credit counts from is not stated in the saved sources; the plan treats it as paid October 15, 2026. A person confirms both.

Unsigned plan. Nothing has been paid or scheduled: $18,308.87 on December 15, 2026, about $22,897.06 on March 15, 2027 and about $17,501.36 on June 15, 2027, all EFTPS, Form 1120, tax period 06/2027, estimated tax. Paying the annualized amounts leaves about $9,217.70 due October 15, 2027 on the projected tax of $71,087.69; the board may prefer the regular amounts for cash planning. The projection changes as each quarter closes.
